subject: DPA: FinTrust onboarding — redlines, retention carve-outs, and signature routing
messages:
From: Marc Sullivan <marc.sullivan@fintrust.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legalops@fintrust.com>, Procurement <procurement@fintrust.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA: FinTrust onboarding — initial redlines

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the walkthrough this morning — excited to move forward. Attached is our initial set of redlines to Redwood's standard DPA (see FinTrust_DPA_v1_redline.pdf). High level asks from our side:

- Data retention carve-out for certain audit logs (we need 7 years for transaction logs per regulator)
- A narrower subprocessor list and requirement for prior notice for new EU-based subprocessors
- Clarification on access to customer data for support engineers (we'd like a written approval flow)

We're trying to keep the process simple: legal review, a short exec approval for carve-outs, then e-signature. Who at Redwood should we expect to sign (company-level vs. regional legal)? Also please confirm if you can provide SOC2 evidence and the SCCs appendix referenced on page 3.

Cc'ing Legal Ops (internal) and Procurement for timeline. We'd like to get this wrapped in the week of Jul 28 if possible.

Thanks,
Marc Sullivan
Head of Legal Operations
FinTrust, Inc.

Attachments: FinTrust_DPA_v1_redline.pdf (pdf), SCCs_Appendix_FINTRUST.docx (docx)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marc Sullivan <marc.sullivan@fintrust.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: FinTrust onboarding — initial redlines

Marc — appreciate the redlines and clear asks. Looping in Neha (Legal) and Laura (Privacy) who will own the review and SCCs evidence. Quick notes before we dive in:

- Retention: we generally default to shorter retention for telemetry and logs, but we do support exceptions for regulated customers on a case-by-case basis. Need to confirm cost/responsibility for extended storage and whether the retention applies to aggregated metrics vs. raw transaction logs.
- Subprocessors: we can provide a current list and agree on notice for EU-based additions; some low-level infra providers are shared across customers. We can explore a monthly notice cadence or a 30-day notice + opt-out window for sensitive regs.
- Support access: we can formalize an approval flow and require Just-in-Time (JIT) access with audit logs; Laura can outline controls and evidence.

Neha/Laura — can you review the attached redline and propose edits on the carve-out language? Also indicate if the SCCs appendix we provide is the standard Redwood package or needs any FinTrust-specific addenda.

Marc — for signature routing, our preferred path for this level of changes is: Legal Ops (Redwood) + FinTrust countersign via DocuSign. If an exec-level exception is needed (e.g., retention 7 years), that will require VP-level approval at Redwood and may take a day or two. We can start the legal redline work immediately.

Karthik
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marc Sullivan <marc.sullivan@fintrust.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 10:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: FinTrust onboarding — initial redlines

Thanks — I've reviewed the redlines. Summary of proposed Redwood responses (high level):

- Retention carve-out: Acceptable to offer a 7-year retention for specific transaction logs, conditional on FinTrust covering incremental storage costs and confirming exact log types (schema). I'll draft language that limits scope to "transactional audit logs" and excludes model training or aggregated analytics.
- Subprocessors: We'll insert a clause to provide an updated subprocessor list quarterly and a 30-day notice for new EU-based subprocessors. We will not agree to a blanket opt-out right, but will add an escalation path for particularly sensitive additions.
- Support access: We'll add a JIT access requirement with documented approval steps and mandatory audit log retention for access events (90 days by default; extendable if required).

Next steps: I'm attaching an annotated DPA with proposed edits (redline integrated) and a draft SCCs appendix that maps to the controls FinTrust requested. Can you confirm if the proposed language on cost allocation for extended retention is acceptable?

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_response_redline.pdf (pdf), Redwood_SCCs_Appendix_v2.docx (docx)

-Neha
Sr. Counsel, Contracts & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Marc Sullivan <marc.sullivan@fintrust.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legalops@fintrust.com>, Procurement <procurement@fintrust.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jul 2025 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: FinTrust onboarding — initial redlines

Neha, Karthik — this looks good and moves in the right direction. A few clarifications from our procurement team:

- Cost for retention: FinTrust prefers a fixed price addon rather than variable storage billing. Can Redwood provide a 12-month fixed fee estimate for the additional storage (we can negotiate if needed)?
- SCCs appendix: Procurement asks that the SCCs appendix explicitly list the FedRAMP-equivalent controls we require for some of our regulated products (we'll attach a short checklist).
- Signature flow: Fine with DocuSign. Please confirm who will be the Redwood signer (name + title) so we can prepare the counterparty signatory block. We want to ensure the signature milestone is the only gating item for go-live — if exec approval is needed, please flag now.

If we can get an estimate and signer info by end of day Friday, Jul 25, procurement will sign off and we can route to DocuSign next week.

Thanks,
Marc

On Wed, Jul 23, 2025 at 08:34 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Marc — noted. If Neha's retention language looks good to you, I can ask Finance to put together a 12-month fixed fee estimate for extended retention and loop in our VP for signoff if required.
>
> Karthik
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marc Sullivan <marc.sullivan@fintrust.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jul 2025 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: FinTrust onboarding — initial redlines

Kevin (cc Karthik/Neha) — quick update from Privacy:

- I've incorporated the FedRAMP-equivalent checklist items into the SCCs appendix and marked three items as "requires attestation" which we can provide via a scoped evidence bundle (SOC2 reports + configuration screenshots).
- Finance provided a ballpark for a 12-month fixed retention fee: $6,500 for 7-year transaction-log retention for the requested volume (subject to final sizing). I'll have a formal quote this afternoon.
- Signer: Redwood will use Neha Kapoor, Sr. Counsel, Contracts & Compliance as our authorized signer for the DPA. If FinTrust needs an exec-level sign, we can escalate, but the current approvals should allow Neha to sign for contract-level DPAs.

I'll post the finalized annotated DPA and SCCs appendix to the HubSpot deal record and send the DocuSign powerform link once we confirm the counterparty signer block.

Laura Bennett
Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference

Related links: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/45832
